title: VSR-Net: Vessel-like Structure Rehabilitation Network with Graph Clustering
mechanism: Takes a coarse vessel mask, groups broken segments into rupture clusters (curvilinear clustering), then merges them across gaps (curvilinear merging) to repair connectivity, with lower calibration error.
evidence: R: five 2D/3D medical datasets; beats prior refinement methods and lowers calibration error (abstract, no numbers on page).
adaptation: Crack channel of the ensemble only: cluster fragments, learn merges across gaps up to about 10 px along local direction; aimed at missed faint segments between detected pieces, scored by relR@2 and component recall. Implementation from paper (code not found).
min_experiment: Arm: VSR-style cluster-and-merge on ensemble crack mask. Baseline: house ensemble. Metric: relR@2 at fixed relP@2, components>=20 px found. Kill: relR@2 < +0.01.
prior_overlap: none. Skeleton Recall and clDice losses were run (training losses), not a post-hoc connectivity refiner.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply to crack components: 76-88% of crack components are < 20 px, many are pieces of one crack; merge collinear fragments; train on out-of-fold maps.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house ensemble + VSR-Net. Baseline: house ensemble. Metrics: components found, relF1@2, ECE of crack probability on 5-fold CV. Kill: components found < +0.02.
